title: dedicated-autoscaler-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
description:
Motivation: Improve observability and accounting of burst capacity usage for Dedicated fleets to help SREs and capacity planners reconcile costs and SLA guarantees. This change adds per-fleet burst allocation tracking, extra telemetry for token-bucket take/release events, and a new utilization report that attributes burst consumption by customer, priority class, and timeframe.

What I changed: consolidated burst accounting into a single service-backed store, emitted structured events for token-bucket operations, and added a nightly aggregation job that writes summarized utilization to the reporting dataset. Also extended the Console dashboards with a new "Burst Utilization" panel and added an opt-in feature flag to enable high-cardinality reporting for customers who request finer-grained attribution.

Checklist:
- [x] Add token-bucket event schema and producer in autoscaler runtime
- [x] Persist per-fleet burst allocations and current usage in persistent store with efficient TTLs
- [x] Implement nightly aggregation job and backfill 7 days for pilot fleets
- [x] Console dashboard updates + Grafana panels
- [x] Unit and integration tests for new aggregation and edge cases (clock skew, partial failures)
- [x] Docs: admin guide for enabling high-cardinality reporting and cost impact notes

Testing and rollout: Unit and integration tests passed in CI. We ran a 48h pilot on two internal fleets (staging) to validate metrics fidelity and storage impact. Backfill job validated against existing billing traces. Rollout plan is staged: enable reporting by default for internal/export flights, opt-in for customer orgs in first week, then enabled by default after monitoring window and SLO validation.

Related: ENG-3421 (autoscaler observability epic), ENG-3619 (burst accounting design). This PR is scoped to the reporting/telemetry path only and does not change the runtime throttling behavior (no breaking changes to request path).
author: Samira Patel
ci_details: Checks: unit (pass), integration (pass), lint (pass), e2e-grafana (pass), storage-migration (pass). All required checks green after one rerun of flaky aggregation test.
commits: consolidate: move burst accounting to dedicated-burst-store service
reports: nightly aggregator for burst utilization summaries
console: add burst utilization dashboard and grafana panel
docs: admin guide for burst reporting
review_comments: Jordan Lee: Can we avoid an extra API call on the hot path by bundling emission with the existing metrics flush?
Samira Patel: Good call — I added a buffered emitter to batch token-bucket events and wired it into the existing metrics flush, see commit 3
Diego Martinez: Aggregator looks good but please add defensive handling for partial day windows and clock skew — otherwise we risk double-counting during DST shifts.
Samira Patel: Added clock-skew windowing and unit tests, plus a backfill dry-run mode to validate before commit.
release_notes: Improved Dedicated autoscaler observability: adds burst allocation tracking, token-bucket events, and nightly utilization reports. Console dashboard added. Opt-in high-cardinality reporting for customers. No runtime throttling changes.
notes_for_ops: Nightly aggregator requires an extra read quota on reporting-store; recommend increasing reporter role rate limit by 20% during initial rollout. Backfill can be disabled via --no-backfill flag if storage pressure is high.
performance_considerations: High-cardinality mode increases event emissions; flagged as opt-in. Batched emission implemented to minimize  p95 latency impact on autoscaler metrics flush. Aggregator job runs off-peak and uses incremental windowing to avoid hot scans.
security_considerations: No new surface exposed to tenants. Burst attribution uses internal IDs only; opt-in detailed attribution requires admin consent. Events are written to existing telemetry topic with existing ACLs.
follow_up: Rollout: enable opt-in for 5 pilot customers and monitor storage/cost for 14 days
Post-rollout: evaluate enabling default high-cardinality for enterprise orgs after pilot
